english.html: recognised on the body of Martin Guerre: it will be answered that a part of these signs, such as the warts on the hands, the drops of blood in the eye, and the sinking of the nail, are each proved by only one witness, and thus they are singular witnesses, who make no proof even though they were a thousand, each deposing to his own fact.

notes.citation: Jacobus Butrigarius (Giacomo Bottrigari, c. 1274–1348, Iaques Butrigaire) on Code 1.5 (De haereticis et Manichaeis et Samaritis), l. Arriani (C. 1.5.5, Theodosius II and Valentinian III, the law against the Arians, Macedonians and other sects)
notes.original: Iaques Butrigaire en la l. Arriani. c. de hæred.
notes.gloss: Butrigarius there on the proof of heresy by witnesses who depose to different heresies; the print's hæred. is hæret.

english.html: In the matter of proofs and of witnesses, it is certain and settled that singular witnesses prove nothing <sup class="mk" data-key="a">a</sup>, even though they were a hundred thousand in number <sup class="mk" data-key="b">b</sup>; for each deposes particularly to his own fact, and thus they hold the place of but one; and the deposition of one, of whatever dignity, greatness or authority he may be, is counted for nothing <sup class="mk" data-key="c">c</sup>: which Cicero in a certain place discourses upon and shows elegantly <sup class="mk" data-key="d">d</sup>. It is quite true that in certain cases singular witnesses (according to the interpretation of several) may [prove] sufficiently: as if it is a question of proving infamy, madness, heresy, or an act in general <sup class="mk" data-key="e">e</sup>; or else of proving an act to whose essence neither place nor time is required, such as a jurisdiction, a choice of burial, rumour and repute <sup class="mk" data-key="f">f</sup>. Whence several have, I know not how, thought that to convict a man of heresy two witnesses suffice, even though one of them should depose to one kind of heresy [and the other to another]: heresies, they say, although they are designated by divers names, are nevertheless interlinked and conjoined in wickedness <sup class="mk" data-key="h">h</sup>. But such an opinion could not be sustained, nor founded upon any text of law, although some (says Panormitanus), by a light and too inconsiderate interpretation, have written to the contrary <sup class="mk" data-key="i">i</sup>. And still less is it true that, to prove a universal or general act, singular witnesses suffice <sup class="mk" data-key="k">k</sup>: for custom in itself is a universal act, regarding all those

notes.citation: Digest 22.5 (De testibus), l. Ob carmen (the print's ob carnem), § Si (cf. D. 22.5.21, Arcadius Charisius, whose § 1 treats witnesses of equal standing who differ; paragraph unverified); Decretals, X 1.6 (De electione et electi potestate), c. Bonae [memoriae], the first so named (chapter number unverified); Decretals, X 2.20 (De testibus et attestationibus), c. Licet ex quadam (cf. X 2.20.47, Innocent III; number unverified)
notes.original: l. ob carnem P ſi D. de te ſti. C. bonæ. l. j. de elect. c. li cet ex quadã. de teſti.
notes.gloss: The texts on which the rule that singular witnesses make no proof is founded; c. Licet ex quadam is the chapter on witnesses who depose from hearsay, cited at annot-052 and annot-053. The P. stands for the paragraph sign; the margin's C. before bonæ is c., capitulum.

notes.citation: Code 4.20 (De testibus), l. Iurisiurandi (C. 4.20.9, Constantine), and Baldus (Balde) there; the § Si cited above at {a}
notes.original: l. Iuriſiurãdi. & illec de Balde. C de te ſti. P. ſi. preal legue.
notes.gloss: C. 4.20.9: witnesses are to be sworn before they testify, and credit given rather to the more honourable; and "we manifestly ordain that the answer of a single witness be not heard at all, even though he shine with the honour of the illustrious senate" — the unus testis nullus testis rule which Coras paraphrases in the next clause.

notes.citation: Digest 48.18 (De quaestionibus), l. Maritus (cf. D. 48.18.17, Papinian; number unverified); l. Iurisiurandi (C. 4.20.9) and c. Licet (X 2.20.47), cited above
notes.original: l. maritus. D. de quæſtio l. Iuriſiurand & c. licet. alle gué.
notes.gloss: The deposition of one, whatever his dignity, is of no account: C. 4.20.9's etiamsi praeclarae curiae honore praefulgeat.

notes.citation: Cicero, Pro M. Fonteio (§§ 21–36, on the Gallic witnesses against Fonteius)
notes.original: Ciceron en l'oraiſon pro M. fonteio.
notes.gloss: Cicero argues that witnesses are to be weighed, not counted — the multitude and unanimity of hostile Gauls proving nothing against a Roman.

notes.citation: Innocent IV on Decretals, X 5.1 (De accusationibus, inquisitionibus et denunciationibus), the second chapter Qualiter et quando (X 5.1.24, Innocent III, the Fourth Lateran Council's canon on inquisition); Baldus (Balde) on Code 5.69 (Qui numero tutelarum se excusant), l. 1 (C. 5.69.1; title identification probable, bearing unverified)
notes.original: Innocent au c. qualiter c. ij. de accu. Balde en la l. j. C. qui num. tutel.
notes.gloss: Innocent IV on the proof of infamia by singular witnesses, which founds an inquisition.

notes.citation: Gui Pape (Guido Papa, d. 1487), Decisiones (of the Parlement of Grenoble), question 154
notes.original: Guid. Papæ en ſes deſi- ſions. q. cliiij.
notes.gloss: On acts to whose essence neither place nor time belongs, which singular witnesses may prove: jurisdiction, choice of burial, repute.

notes.citation: Code 1.5 (De haereticis et Manichaeis et Samaritis), l. Quicumque, at the verse Idcirco (cf. C. 1.5.4, Arcadius and Honorius, on the Manichaeans and Donatists; number unverified); a chapter printed c. Pan. in the same title of the Liber Sextus (VI 5.2, De haereticis) — unidentified, unless Pan. is Panormitanus on the title
notes.original: l. quicũque. verſi Idcirco. C. de hæret. c. Pan. au meſme titre du vj
notes.gloss: The opinion that all heresies, under divers names, are one wickedness, so that two witnesses deposing to different heresies concur.

notes.citation: Panormitanus (Niccolò de' Tudeschi, Panorme), Consilia, consilium 42 of the first volume
notes.original: Panorme au cõſil xlij. du j. Volume.
notes.gloss: Panormitanus rejects the opinion as founded on no text and on a light and inconsiderate interpretation; Coras quotes him.

notes.citation: Decretum, C. 3 q. 9, c. Nihilominus (canon number unverified), or the Gloss there
notes.original: c. nihilomi nus. ou auſſi la Gloſ. iij. q. ix.
notes.gloss: On the number and concurrence of witnesses required in criminal causes.

lines: recogneuës au corps de Martin Guerre:
ſera reſpõdu qu'vne partie de ces ſignes,
comme des verrues des mains, goutes de
ſang à l'œil, & enfoncement de l'ongle,
ne ſont prouuees chacune que par vn
teſmoin, & par ainſi ce ſont teſmoins ſin-
guliers qui ne font preuue encor qu'ils
fuſſent mille, depoſans chacun de ſon
En matierre de preuues, & de teſmoins. il eſt cer-
tain & reſolu que teſmoins ſinguliers ne preuuent
poinct {a}, bien qu'ils fuſſent cent mille en nombre {b}. car
chacun depoſa particulierement de ſon faict, & par
ainſi ne tiennent le lieu que d'vn: & la depoſition d'vn
de quelque dignité, grandeur, ou authorité qu'il ſoit,
n'eſt pour rien comptee {c}: Ce que Ciceron en quelque
lieu dilcourt, & remonſtre elegãment {d}. Il eſt bien vray
qu'en certains cas, les teſmoins ſinguliers (ſelon l'in-
terpretation de pluſieurs) peuuent ſuffiſamment: cõme
ſ'il ſ'agiſt de prouuer l'infamie, fureur, hereſie ou vn
acte en general {e}, Ou bien de prouuer vn acte, à l'eſſẽce
duquel n'eſt deſiré, ni lieu, ni temps, comme eſt vne
iuriſdiction, election de ſepulture, bruit & fame {f}.
Dont pluſieurs ont ie ne ſçay comment penſé, qu'à cõ-
uaincre vn homme heretique ſuffiſent deux teſmoins,
bien qne l'vn d'eux depoſent d'vne eſpece d'hereſies,
diſent ils, combien que ſoyent par diuers noms deſi-
gnées, ſont neantmoins entreliees, & coniontes en
meſchancetè {h}. Mais telle opinion ne ſe pourroit ſou-
ſtenir, ni fonder par aucun texte de droit, quoy que
quelques vns (dit Panorme) par interpretation legiere,
& trop inconſiderée, ayant eſcrit au contraire {i}. Et
moins eſt veritable, qu'à prouuer vn acte vniuerſel,
ou general, teſmoins ſinguliers ſuffiſent {k}. car couſtu-
me en ſoy, eſt vn acte vniuerſel, regardant tous ceux

readings.reason: c. ij. = capitulum, 'the second chapter Qualiter [et quando]' (X 5.1.24); the unread sort in B has no better candidate.
Balde = Baldus, the authority cited on l. j. C. qui num. tutel.; B only leaves the first letter unread.

en ſes deſiſions = 'in his Decisions' (Gui Pape); reading A is complete and legible, B leaves a letter unread; one line, one choice with p080-m5l1-2.; deſi-ſions/desi-ſions are both decisions; same line as p080-m5l1-1, so the same choice (A), reading A being the complete line.
nihilominus is the chapter's incipit (c. Nihilominus, repeated in note ſ); nibilominus is a wrong sort (h read as b).
iij. q. ix. = Causa 3, quaestio 9 of the Decretum; Causa 2 has only eight quaestiones, so ij. q. ix. cannot exist.
